# Siren core — parse-to-animated-render skeleton (step-reveal slice)

## Problem

Siren is a new, open-source (MIT), Mermaid-syntax-aligned diagram renderer whose whole point is
authoring declarative animation (step reveal, highlighting, enter/exit transitions) *inside the
same plain-text document* as the diagram — copy the document, paste it wherever the renderer is
loaded, and it plays. No such tool exists today: Mermaid itself has two long-open, unclaimed
feature requests for this (mermaid-js/mermaid#7710, #3029); the closest prior art either
post-processes Mermaid's already-rendered SVG from the outside (mermaid-animate, reveal-md
fragments) or is a closed SaaS that converts Mermaid into a GIF/video (FlowGif, fanfa.dev). None
of them give the diagram author a single self-contained text format with fine-grained,
CSS-like control over individual element timing.

Nothing has been built yet — this repository is empty. Before any syntax or effect can be
designed further, the full pipeline (text in → animated DOM out) needs to exist end to end, even
in its smallest possible form, so every later slice (more effects, more diagram types, more
syntax) extends a working skeleton instead of a pile of disconnected prototypes.

## Outcome

A developer can write a single `.siren` (or inline `<pre class="siren">`) text document containing:
- a minimal Mermaid-style flowchart (nodes + directed edges), and
- a `timeline:` block that assigns nodes/edges to numbered steps with an `enter fade` action,

pass that text to `render(source, container)` from `@siren/core`, and see a correctly laid-out
SVG flowchart mounted into the DOM where step-1 elements are visible immediately and every later
step's elements start hidden and fade in on each `controller.next()` call. This is verifiable two
ways: automated tests against the module seams, and a browser demo page a human can click through.

## Scope

- A hand-written parser for a minimal flowchart-only subset of Mermaid syntax: `flowchart TD|LR`
  header, node declarations (`A[Label]`, standalone or inline on an edge), directed edges
  (`A --> B`), and a `timeline:` block (`step N: enter <id> fade[, enter <id> fade ...]`).
- A graph-model stage that resolves and validates the parsed document (unknown ids referenced in
  `timeline:`, duplicate node ids) into a normalized in-memory graph with a resolved timeline.
- A layout engine that computes node positions/sizes and edge paths using `@dagrejs/dagre`
  internally for rank/position assignment, behind our own `layoutGraph()` interface, with an
  injectable text-measurement seam.
- An SVG renderer that builds the DOM tree (rects/text for nodes, paths/markers for edges) with
  stable, documented id/class conventions that later modules (and later slices) can rely on.
- An animation runtime that initializes step>1 elements as hidden and exposes a step controller
  (`next`/`reset`) that reveals one step at a time via a CSS class toggle (fade only, in v1).
- A public `render(source, container)` entry point composing all of the above, returning the SVG,
  the controller, and any diagnostics — mirroring Mermaid's low-ceremony usage pattern.
- A browser demo page, built against the real Vite library bundle, with Next/Reset buttons.
- Monorepo scaffolding: pnpm workspace, `packages/core` (published as `@siren/core`, MIT license).

## Non-goals

- Any diagram type other than flowchart (sequence, class, state, etc.) — deferred.
- Any node shape other than a plain rectangle, and any edge style other than a plain solid arrow
  (no labels on edges yet, no dotted/thick lines, no subgraphs) — deferred.
- Any animation effect other than `enter fade` — no `exit`, no `highlight`, no slide, no custom
  easing/duration authoring — deferred to later slices, once this skeleton is proven.
- Autoplay / timers / scroll-triggered playback — `next()` is caller-driven only in this slice.
- Edge-crossing minimization or layout quality tuning beyond dagre's defaults.
- `Siren.init()` DOM auto-scanning (à la Mermaid's `<pre class="mermaid">` auto-render) — the
  public seam for this slice is the explicit `render()` call only.
- Parser error recovery / partial-parse tolerance beyond returning a diagnostics array.
- VSCode extension, website, playground — separate projects, not touched here.
- Splitting the parser into its own publishable package (Mermaid does this) — everything lives in
  `packages/core` until the grammar is proven; splitting is a mechanical move for later.

## Domain decisions

- **Step**: a positive integer named in the `timeline:` block. Steps are revealed in ascending
  order via `controller.next()`. A node or edge never mentioned in `timeline:` is visible from the
  start (implicit "step 0") — authors are not required to place every element on the timeline.
- **Enter effect**: the action a pending element performs when its step is revealed. v1 defines
  exactly one: `fade`. Any other effect name in `timeline:` is a diagnostic error, not a crash.
- **Node id**: the identifier token from flowchart syntax (`A`, `B`, ...), first-label-wins if the
  same id is declared with conflicting bracket text (a diagnostic warning is recorded, not an
  error).
- **Edge id**: auto-generated as `${fromId}-${toId}`; a second edge between the same pair becomes
  `${fromId}-${toId}#2`, etc. `timeline:` references edges by this id.
- **Diagnostic**: `{ severity: 'error' | 'warning', message: string, line?: number, column?: number }`.
  Diagnostics are returned, never thrown, except for truly unexpected internal errors (bugs).
  `render()` still returns a result object (with an empty/partial SVG) when there are error-level
  diagnostics — it does not throw.
- **SVG conventions** (frozen now so renderer and animation-runtime tickets can be built and
  tested independently of each other):
  - Every node is a `<g class="siren-node" data-siren-id="{id}">` containing a `<rect>` + `<text>`.
  - Every edge is a `<path class="siren-edge" data-siren-id="{id}" marker-end="url(#siren-arrow)">`.
  - An element referenced anywhere in `timeline:` (step 1 included — `next()` is what reveals
    step 1 too, there is no separate "reveal step 0" call) starts with an additional
    `siren-pending` class. Only elements never mentioned in `timeline:` (implicit step 0) start
    without it. (Corrected during round 2: the original wording said "step > 1", which would
    leave step-1 elements visible before any `next()` call — inconsistent with `next()` being the
    only thing that reveals step 1. Tickets 04 and 05 both independently implemented "any
    timeline entry" and agree with each other; this line is the fix to match them.)
  - Revealing a step removes `siren-pending` and adds `siren-enter-fade` to that step's elements.
  - Label text is always set via `textContent`, never `innerHTML` — labels are untrusted
    author input and must never be interpreted as markup/HTML (this is a hard invariant, not a
    nice-to-have; Mermaid itself runs everything through DOMPurify for the same reason).

## Design contract

### `packages/core/src/contracts.ts` (shared type contracts, no logic)

- Responsibilities: hold every cross-module interface type agreed above (`SirenDocument`,
  `Diagnostic`, `GraphModel`, `ResolvedTimeline`, `PositionedGraph`, `TextMeasurer`,
  `AnimationController`, etc.) so downstream tickets can implement and test against a frozen
  shape without waiting on each other's implementations.
- Non-responsibilities: no functions, no logic — types and JSDoc only.
- Interface: pure TypeScript type/interface exports.
- Seam: this file *is* the seam that unlocks parallel work — every other module treats it as
  read-only after ticket 01 lands.
- Dependencies: none.

### Parser (`packages/core/src/parser/`)

- Responsibilities: `parseSiren(source: string): { document: SirenDocument | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }`.
  Recognizes the flowchart header, node/edge declarations, and the `timeline:` block described
  above; reports syntax diagnostics without throwing on malformed input.
- Non-responsibilities: does not check that timeline references point at real nodes/edges (that's
  the graph model's job); no layout, no rendering.
- Interface: `parseSiren(source: string): ParseResult`. Pure function, no I/O, no DOM.
- Seam: `parseSiren` itself — string in, data out.
- Dependencies: none (hand-written lexer/parser; grammar is small enough that a parser-generator
  dependency isn't justified yet).

### Graph model (`packages/core/src/graph-model/`)

- Responsibilities: `buildGraphModel(document: SirenDocument): { graph: GraphModel | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }`.
  Assigns edge ids, resolves every `timeline:` reference against declared node/edge ids, flags
  duplicate node ids and unresolved timeline references as error diagnostics.
- Non-responsibilities: no coordinates, no rendering, no animation.
- Interface: `buildGraphModel(document: SirenDocument): GraphModelResult`. Pure function.
- Seam: `buildGraphModel` itself; testable with hand-built `SirenDocument` fixtures, independent
  of the real parser.
- Dependencies: none.

### Layout (`packages/core/src/layout/`)

- Responsibilities: `layoutGraph(graph: GraphModel, options: LayoutOptions): PositionedGraph`.
  Assigns x/y/width/height per node and a point path per edge, using `@dagrejs/dagre` internally
  for rank/position computation (`rankdir` mapped from the flowchart's `TD`/`LR` direction), and
  an injected `TextMeasurer` for label sizing.
- Non-responsibilities: no SVG, no styling, no animation.
- Interface: `layoutGraph(graph: GraphModel, options: { measureText: TextMeasurer }): PositionedGraph`.
- Seam: the `TextMeasurer` injection point (`{ measure(text): { width, height } }`) — production
  uses a canvas/DOM-based measurer wired in the demo; tests use a deterministic fake
  (`width = text.length * charWidth`) so layout output is snapshot-stable without a browser.
- Dependencies: `@dagrejs/dagre` (production, real — it's a pure, deterministic computation
  library; running it for real in tests is fine, no fake needed).

### Renderer (`packages/core/src/renderer/`)

- Responsibilities: `renderToSVG(graph: PositionedGraph): SVGSVGElement`. Builds the SVG DOM tree
  per the frozen SVG conventions above, including the initial `siren-pending` class on step>1
  elements (it needs the resolved timeline, carried on `PositionedGraph`, to know which elements
  start pending).
- Non-responsibilities: does not decide *when* to reveal a step, does not attach playback
  controls or event listeners.
- Interface: `renderToSVG(graph: PositionedGraph): SVGSVGElement`.
- Seam: the DOM itself — tests run under Vitest's jsdom environment (a real DOM implementation,
  not a mock) and assert on the constructed tree's structure/attributes; the demo page runs the
  same code in a real browser DOM.
- Dependencies: DOM global (jsdom in tests, browser in the demo — both real, locally substitutable
  implementations of the same interface).

### Animation runtime (`packages/core/src/animation/`)

- Responsibilities: `createAnimationController(svg: SVGSVGElement, timeline: ResolvedTimeline): AnimationController`
  where `AnimationController = { totalSteps: number; currentStep: number; next(): void; reset(): void }`.
  `next()` finds elements tagged for `currentStep + 1`, removes `siren-pending`, adds
  `siren-enter-fade` (a class with a CSS transition defined in the shipped stylesheet), and
  advances `currentStep`. Calling `next()` past the last step is a no-op. `reset()` restores the
  initial pending state and `currentStep = 0`.
- Non-responsibilities: no other effects, no autoplay/timers — v1 is caller-driven only.
- Interface: `createAnimationController(svg, timeline): AnimationController`.
- Seam: DOM class-list state, observable synchronously after each call — no dependency on real
  CSS transition timing being supported in the test environment (jsdom doesn't fully implement
  CSS animation timing; tests verify *state transitions*, not smoothness — visual smoothness is
  what the demo page is for).
- Dependencies: DOM only.

### Public API (`packages/core/src/index.ts`)

- Responsibilities: `render(source: string, container: HTMLElement): SirenRenderResult` where
  `SirenRenderResult = { svg: SVGSVGElement | null; controller: AnimationController | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }`.
  Runs parse → buildGraphModel → layoutGraph → renderToSVG → createAnimationController, mounts the
  SVG into `container` on success, and returns the aggregated diagnostics either way.
- Non-responsibilities: no DOM auto-scanning/auto-init (explicitly out of scope this slice).
- Interface: `render(source: string, container: HTMLElement): SirenRenderResult`.
- Seam: this is the primary end-to-end integration seam — acceptance criteria are tested here.
- Dependencies: composes the modules above; a real `HTMLElement` container is required (jsdom in
  tests).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid source (flowchart + a `timeline:` block with 2+ steps) → `render()` mounts an SVG into
      `container` with one `<g class="siren-node">` per declared node and one
      `<path class="siren-edge">` per declared edge, each carrying `data-siren-id` matching its
      declared/generated id.
- [ ] Elements referenced anywhere in `timeline:` start with the `siren-pending` class; elements never mentioned
      in `timeline:` start without it (visible immediately).
- [ ] `controller.totalSteps` equals the highest step number declared in `timeline:` (0 when there
      is no `timeline:` block at all, and every element renders immediately visible).
- [ ] Calling `controller.next()` removes `siren-pending` and adds `siren-enter-fade` on exactly
      the elements assigned to the newly revealed step, and increments `controller.currentStep`.
- [ ] Calling `controller.next()` at the last step is a no-op — no error, `currentStep` unchanged.
- [ ] Calling `controller.reset()` restores every step>1 element to `siren-pending` (removing
      `siren-enter-fade`) and sets `controller.currentStep` back to 0.
- [ ] A `timeline:` entry referencing an undeclared node/edge id produces an error-severity
      diagnostic; `render()` returns it in `diagnostics` and does not throw.
- [ ] Node/edge label text is inserted via `textContent` only — a label containing
      `<script>`/HTML-looking text renders as literal visible text, never as markup.
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.html`, opened in a browser and built against the real `@siren/core`
      Vite library bundle, visibly fades in nodes one at a time as a human clicks "Next", and
      resets on "Reset".

## Test strategy

- `parseSiren` — unit, pure function, no environment.
- `buildGraphModel` — unit, pure function, hand-built `SirenDocument` fixtures.
- `layoutGraph` — unit, pure function, fake deterministic `TextMeasurer`.
- `renderToSVG` — component test under Vitest's jsdom environment (real DOM, not a mock),
  hand-built `PositionedGraph` fixtures.
- `createAnimationController` — component test under jsdom, hand-built SVG + `ResolvedTimeline`
  fixtures matching the frozen SVG conventions.
- `render()` — integration test under jsdom, exercising the full pipeline for every acceptance
  criterion above except the last (the demo page is verified manually/visually in a real browser;
  automated browser e2e via Playwright is explicitly deferred to a later slice).

## Verification

- Focused: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test -- <file>`
- Suite: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test`
- Static: `pnpm --filter @siren/core exec tsc --noEmit`

(Exact script names are established by ticket 01, which creates `packages/core/package.json`;
this is the intended shape.)

## Baseline

Measured 2026-09-03. The repository is empty (no `package.json`, no source, no tests exist yet).
Baseline is vacuous: 0 pre-existing failing tests, 0 pre-existing type errors, because there is
nothing to fail yet.

## Risks and deferred questions

- The `timeline:` block syntax is our own invention, not derived from any existing spec — expect
  it to need revision once `exit`/`highlight`/slide effects are designed in a later slice. Treated
  as an intentionally provisional decision, not a frozen one.
- `@dagrejs/dagre` is the actively maintained fork of the original `dagre` (which Mermaid itself
  also depends on, via `dagre-d3-es`); pinning this now avoids ambiguity later.
- Parallelism note: tickets 02–05 (graph-model, layout, renderer, animation) are only safely
  parallel because ticket 01 freezes every cross-module type in `contracts.ts` first. If that
  contract turns out to be wrong once integration (ticket 06) happens, fixing it fans across all
  four tickets — recorded as a known risk of the interface-first approach, not hidden.
- Sanitization is scoped to "never use innerHTML for label text" in this slice. A fuller review
  (e.g. attribute-injection edge cases) is deferred until more syntax surface exists.
